header: THE BYTES OF A PDF, AS A PLAIN COPY, FOR pdf-parse. pdf-parse (1.1.1, last released in 2018) carries an old pdf.js (1.10.100). On Node 24 that engine fails at random (about 4 reads in 10: "bad XRef entry", "Illegal character: 41") when it is handed a Node Buffer, and never fails when it is handed a plain Uint8Array holding the same bytes (36 of 36 reads, measured on Node 24.22 with two PDFs; Node 22 reads both forms every time). The copy costs one pass over the file and changes nothing on Node 22, so I send every call of pdf-parse through here (src/lib/pdf/plainBytes.selftest.ts checks that none forgets). pdf-to-img (a current pdfjs-dist) was measured on the same Node and reads a Buffer every time, so it does not need this.
behaviours: the copy is a plain Uint8Array, not a Buffer, with the same bytes
it is a copy: changing it leaves the original alone
an empty input gives an empty copy
the places that load pdf-parse are the three known ones (a new one must be added here and use plainBytes)
${c}: every pdf-parse call is given plainBytes(...)
24 reads of the test PDF through plainBytes() all give both pages and the text
